brief: #189's own surprise is an unfixed bug, and this domain is 11 iterations back — the longest untouched. Two seeds of six saw 0 wet ticks of 1685 between the martins arriving and leaving (no rain at all in that season) and those eaves stayed bare for the town's whole first year. The colony is the newest life system in the town and in a third of worlds it never happens at all. wetF() gates the mud that builds a nest and rain is the ONLY source of mud in the model. Price it first over 6 seeds x 2 years (probes/mart-mud.mjs exists): what fraction of worlds reach the plateau, and what the wet integral is in each. Then give the birds a second source that is not a coin the weather flips — water the birds can reach is wet whatever the sky is doing (the margin, SHOAL, the lap, the pond, the fountain), or mud lives on the ground and DRIES rather than existing only while it is raining.
successLooksLike: 6 of 6 seeds reach a colony in year one. The curve keeps its 0 -> plateau -> 0 shape and its empty autumn and late winter, the clustered mean run stays in 9.7..16.3 against a uniform control's 1.26..1.78, and 0 of the clinging birds are off a nest.
avoid: Do not widen the season, and do not simply lower the mud threshold — that makes the WET years denser as well as saving the dry ones, and #189 tuned the plateau against the eave line's 217 cells. The fix is a SOURCE, not a constant. Keep the CA's shape: zero R(), founder x creep x ceiling.
